When I made Arbiter guns, I set out for one major design concept, making them unique from bows and crossbows (rather than just reskinns, or just upgrades).  So in tier one, average combat is 3 rounds and tier 2 average combat is 5 (base game)

So any weapon that can be used 5 times or more, generally wont need reloading unless someone gets extra attacks.  Most players frontload damage, so if they have an option of a little for 5 rounds, or a lot of 2 or 3, they will pick the two or three.

So what i did was say, guns take 1 minute to reload (thus effectively cant be reloaded in combat).  Being someone that regularly shoots guns, 1 minute is a fair reload time.  Then if damage is better than a longbow, it needs to have a cost.

Look at the gun I designed for this season, The base damage is the revolver damage (casue I didnt want it to be a step back compared to other firearm base damages), along with it burning spells slots.  Damage is based on DMG custom spell damage (tho instead of aoes having ~2d6 per level, i did 1d10 which is the single target damage or healing).

So overall its a single cone shot, with just slightly better than bow damage so its on par with the firearms we use, uses an attunement slot, and for the cost of aspell slot does damage roughtly on par with spells you would use at those levels (lvl 1 and 2 slots are better, lvl 3 is abotu the same, and everything else is a bit less)

Secel gets up from her napping spot against an unused headstone. Stretching out, she groaned at the stiffness of her joints. Then, after standing up finally, she looked around. Knowing the truth somehow made everything more… wicked. It hurt more than she wanted to believe. 

But despite this, she couldn’t say no to this. She owed it to herself, to the people she had fought to save, the people she had bled for. The ones who would never see the light of day again.

Grabbing hold of a shovel, she began digging. The digging wasn’t the hard part, but the weight was unsettling. Eventually she set up the first line of new graves, and did her best to do the traditions of the countless other religions followed by the thousands upon thousands of deceased. But those who she didn’t know anything about got the burial she had grown up with. 

When it came to the dead British, she allocated a section to them. When it came to the dead soldiers that had saved the city by turning it to ruin, they got their own section. The dead civilians took up the majority.

By the time she finally stopped, she couldn’t help but feel like her task was far, far from over. She then turned to getting the plans for her new home designed. In keeping with tradition, the building would be in the style of the Ancient Greek buildings, with enough space for possibly a small family to live in. Looking down into the hole that was the basement, she sighs and pulls the Demon Armor out of the hole. 

“I think this should work?” She asks out loud before tracing the space with her finger. “Should being the key word. Don’t get your hopes up Secel. Just because you’re doing this doesn’t mean he’ll want you if you tell him.”
